summary: 76-year-old man with high dysphagia in the neck, gurgling, regurgitation of undigested food hours after eating, halitosis and nocturnal cough. Dysphagia is a red flag at any age; contrast (barium) swallow before endoscopy when a pouch is suspected.

inputs.hpi: Eighteen months of food catching high in the neck, a gurgling noise when swallowing, and regurgitating undigested food, sometimes hours after meals. Bad breath. Wakes coughing at night. Lost 3 kg. No hoarseness.

exam.other: Neck: soft fullness on the left that gurgles on palpation after drinking. No lymphadenopathy.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected pharyngeal pouch (Zenker's diverticulum)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: High dysphagia with gurgling, regurgitation of undigested food and halitosis — suspected pharyngeal pouch. Barium swallow before endoscopy.

rationale: High (oropharyngeal) dysphagia with the classic pouch triad. Tests that the dysphagia red flag fires for neck-level dysphagia and that the work-up is a contrast swallow/endoscopy; PANE has no pouch node, so this measures coverage.
